title: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi
summary: Al-Khwarizmi, a scholar at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad under Caliph al-Mamun, wrote the book on al-jabr from which "algebra" takes its name. A Latin version of his treatise on Hindu numerals gave rise to the word "algorithm". He also compiled astronomical tables and a geographical work. His life dates are approximate.

uncertainty.note: Both sources give approximate dates; MacTutor Quick Info says about 780 while its page title says 790-850.

where.modern_name: Baghdad, Iraq (where he worked; birthplace uncertain, possibly Khwarizm)

importance.justification: His algebra treatise and numeral work shaped mathematics; his name gave us the word algorithm.

sources.title: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Musa Al-Khwarizmi
sources.publisher: MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews
sources.author: J J O'Connor and E F Robertson

reviewer_note: Least sure of birth place and year: MacTutor says possibly Baghdad and notes the Khwarizm epithet may refer to ancestors; Encyclopedia.com says probably Iraq. The algebra treatise date (roughly 825-830 per Encyclopedia.com) is not pinned. The pin is Baghdad, where he worked, not his birthplace.
